outcome: Help insurers settle valid claims faster by automating evidence intake, coverage checks, triage, and fraud indicators while keeping material decisions under human control.
overview: Claims teams receive forms, policies, invoices, images, reports and medical or repair evidence across many channels; manual re-keying and repeated information requests delay genuine customers and hide suspicious patterns. This solution extracts and validates claim evidence, checks policy and coverage rules with citations, flags missing information, assigns triage and fraud indicators, and prepares an adjuster summary. Low-risk claims can follow an approved straight-through path; uncertain, high-value or adverse decisions always go to qualified staff. An 8–12-week proof of value targets one product and claim type, aiming for shorter settlement times, lower handling cost, more consistent decisions and reduced leakage.

benefits.text: Reduce low-risk claim cycle time by a target 40–70%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target range to validate against the customer’s claims-core timestamps during the PoV — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Reduce manual intake effort by 30–50% and increase the straight-through share by 20%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on document and image quality and on how much coverage logic is machine-readable

benefits.text: Surface duplicate, inflated or connected suspicious claims earlier without increasing wrongful denial
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Fraud-indicator quality depends on historical SIU labels; every adverse decision remains with qualified staff

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); a hybrid option keeps regulated health or sensitive evidence on customer-approved infrastructure

notFor.situation: Policy wording and coverage rules exist only as unstructured legacy documents nobody can authorise
notFor.why: Coverage checks cite approved policy sources; without an authoritative rule source the system cannot make a defensible coverage statement

notFor.situation: Claim evidence arrives mainly as poor-quality scans or photographs below extraction thresholds
notFor.why: Extraction accuracy drives everything downstream; below-threshold evidence produces rework rather than automation

notFor.situation: The insurer expects automated claim denial
notFor.why: Adverse decisions always route to qualified staff in this design; automating denial is a conduct and regulatory risk the offer excludes

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer retains coverage policy, reserves, fraud referral and settlement authority · Duration: 8–12 weeks PoV; 14–26 weeks to production
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, vendor platform specialist; customer claims sponsor, product/policy owner, SIU lead, data owner, privacy and security approvers, core claims lead, finance and CX · Support model: Business-hours standard with an extended/24×7 option; severity-based targets; partner first line with vendor escalation; optional managed claims operation
1) Discovery, claim-type and rule design
2) Data preparation and extraction benchmark
3) Triage build and integration
4) Quality and security testing
5) Handler training and UAT
6) Controlled launch, stabilisation and handover
